# Chapter 32 — What Was Confirmed and What Was Not: the Ledger of 90 Sub-measures (Chapters 7–31), with Evidence and Negative Findings {#sec-qjax32 .unnumbered}

> **Día de análisis y actualización:** 23 de noviembre de 2026

> **Analysis and update date:** November 23, 2026

> Rewrite of the old Ch. 29 ("confirmed empirical advantages") on the basis of Ch. 1–31. Module: `qang.qledger` (standard library only). Verification: `tools/verify_cap32.py`, which **reads the Appendix H tables of the chapters themselves** and checks that every cited function and verifier exists. This chapter adds no new results: it audits the previous ones.

---

## 32.1 The ledger

Each chapter 7–31 closes with an Appendix H table (id, family, formula, function, status). `qang.qledger` parses them and checks four rules: (1) the statuses belong to the list of `THEORY_CORE.md`; (2) every cited function or `verify_capNN.py` exists in `qang/` or `tools/`; (3) each chapter has its verifier and a test block; (4) ids are unique. Result (`exact`, automatic audit):

| item | value |
|---|---|
| sub-measures | **90** in 25 chapters |
| references checked (functions and verifiers) | 106, **0 unresolved** |
| primary status `exact` | 82 |
| `against` | 3 |
| `no gain` | 3 |
| `mixed` | 1 |
| `unverified` | 1 |
| `measured gain` | **0** |
| `tested on hardware` (primary status) | **0** |
| `exact` **with no caveat at all** | 64 |
| rows with a caveat (hardware, `mixed`, `against`, `no gain`) | 19 |

The ledger is audited automatically from the chapters' own Appendix H tables: 90 sub-measures, 106 references all resolved, 82 `exact`, and **zero** `measured gain`.

## 32.2 Honest reading of the numbers

1. **"Confirmed" here means exact in analysis or in simulation**, not measured on a device. No sub-measure of Ch. 7–31 has `tested on hardware` as its primary status. The only row that cites hardware as a caveat is `readout_drag_affine` (Ch. 25, §168 of the notes). The device-measured advantages of the original treatise live in `RESEARCH_NOTES.md` and are neither reproduced nor extended here.
2. Of the 82 `exact` rows, **18 carry a caveat** (mostly `hardware unverified`): the result is correct, but its transfer to a device was not verified. The remaining 64 have no caveat, and several of them are identities (for example, $F\preceq4g$ with $P=8$, or exact $N$ mod 4 for $N=2,n=4$).
3. Zero `measured gain` means that **no chapter of this rewrite measures a gain against a classical or standard method on real data**; the "without qang vs with qang" comparisons are of resources, of analytic exactness or of simulations.

## 32.4 What was not gained (the 8 non-positive results)

| Ch. | sub-measure | status | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | `plateau_unit_rescale` | `against` | changing unit does not mitigate plateaus |
| 10 | `holonomic_z_area` | `no gain` | no area gain |
| 11 | `ghz_dephasing` | `no gain` | GHZ does not improve under Markovian dephasing |
| 13 | `collective_oscillations` | `unverified` | unverified |
| 15 | `one_basis_bias` | `mixed` | single-basis bound: mixed result |
| 18 | `page_curve_qgS` | `against` | $qg_S$ is flat where the Page curve changes |
| 19 | `pqc_out_of_scope` | `against` | post-quantum cryptography out of scope |
| 30 | `control_quantization_unit` | `no gain` | the unit does not change the rounding error |

To these are added the `no gain` caveats of `unary_sector_kernel` (Ch. 26: classical kernel) and of `qaoa_exact_k_xy` (Ch. 28: the classical greedy reaches 0.977 of the optimum). The methodological conclusion is that of Ch. 31: **register losses together with gains**.

### `tests/test_qledger.py`
```python
from qang.qledger import parse_appendix_h, primary_status, STATUSES, function_names
T = "## 9.9 Appendix H\n\n| id | family | formula | function | status |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| `a` | x | y | `f` | `exact`; hw `unverified` |\n| `b` | x | y | `verify_cap09.py` §4 | `no gain` |\n\n## End\n"
def test_parse(): r = parse_appendix_h(T, 9); assert [x["id"] for x in r] == ["a", "b"]
def test_primary(): r = parse_appendix_h(T, 9); assert primary_status(r[0]["status"]) == "exact" and primary_status(r[1]["status"]) == "no gain"
def test_names(): assert function_names("`verify_cap09.py` §4") == ["verify_cap09.py"] and function_names("`AffineChannel.then`") == ["then"]
def test_status_list(): assert "measured gain" in STATUSES and len(STATUSES) == 8
```
